# Chapter 17: embeddings and vector search

Python 3.10+ standard library only. Extract all four files together. No model download, network, API, or third-party package.

**The vectors and centroids are hand-authored geometry fixtures, not embeddings generated by a trained encoder.** The eight movie summaries, runtimes, and relevance judgments come from Chapter 16. Only the three named queries have vectors; there is no arbitrary-text encoder here.

```powershell
py vector_search.py
py vector_search.py --metric dot
py vector_search.py --metric euclidean --normalization unit
py vector_search.py --mode probe1
py vector_search.py --mode probe2 --limit under120
py vector_search.py --query funny --k 1
py -m unittest -v test_vector_search.py
```

Use `python` or `python3` if appropriate. The script reads `vectors.json` beside itself and prints JSON, without editing files. `--input` overrides the snapshot. Query presets are `space`, `funny`, `quiet`; K is 1-8. Invalid settings/data exit 2 with a JSON error; invalid command syntax uses argparse's usage error. All rows must declare the same `space_id`, have exactly three finite coordinates with absolute value at most 1e6, and norm at least 1e-12.

## Follow the code

1. `validate_snapshot`: verify declared vector-space and catalog contracts. An ID check cannot prove a model really generated its vector.
2. `unit`, `cosine`, `dot`, `distance`: use all three coordinates. Euclidean values include the square root. Descending cosine/dot, ascending distance. Exact ties sort by movie ID.
3. `experiment`: assign each movie to the centroid with highest cosine, breaking ties by centroid ID. Centroids are authored, not fitted. Filter runtime metadata independently; unknown runtime fails a known-runtime requirement.
4. `probe1`, `probe2`, `probe3`: visit the nearest one, two, or three centroids by cosine, then score eligible members. These modes require cosine. Exact mode scores all eligible movies with the chosen metric. This illustrates coarse selection, not HNSW or production IVF performance.
5. Compute a **separate exact audit**, then neighbor recall against that reference. The complete experiment also runs the audit and BM25, so candidate count is not a timing benchmark.
6. Compare relevance with the authored labels. Labels affect evaluation, never vector scoring, cell assignment, or BM25 ranking.

## Expected default output

q = [1,0,0], cosine, raw lengths, no filter, K=3:

- M004 Quiet Orbit: 0.9938837347
- M008 Parallel World: 0.9810229432
- M007 Unlisted Voyage: 0.9701425001

Cell A: M004, M008. B: M001, M002, M003, M005, M007. C: M006. One probe visits A and recovers 2/3 exact neighbors; two probes recover all three. Raw dot ranks M002, M008, M004. Raw Euclidean ranks M004, M007, M008. Unit normalization makes cosine/dot/Euclidean rankings agree, apart from numerical ties.

BM25 uses the Chapter 16 formula (k1=1.2, b=.75), summary-only lowercase `[a-z0-9]+` tokenization, unique query terms, OR matching, full-catalog statistics, and runtime filtering before K. Its default IDs remain M008, M004, M005. Source summary edits do **not** regenerate the authored vectors automatically: that mismatch is a reason to keep vectors and source revisions aligned.

## Evaluation definitions

- Neighbor recall@K = returned IDs shared with the exact top-K / size of that exact set. Undefined (null) if no eligible reference items. It measures search fidelity, not relevance.
- Relevance Precision@K = relevant returned results / requested K. Empty slots count as zero.
- Relevance Recall@K = relevant returned results / relevant eligible count. Undefined (null) if no relevant eligible movies.
- Reciprocal rank@K = 1/(rank of the first relevant top-K result), or zero if absent.

Filtering changes the eligible reference and relevance denominators. For one-cell space search with `under120`, neighbor recall remains 2/3 because the exact third neighbor becomes M003; relevance recall becomes 1 because M007 is no longer eligible. A similarity value is not a probability. This fixture's successful cases do not prove learned-model quality.

To use a real encoder later, replace both query and document vectors using its documented compatible preprocessing, version, dimensionality, and metric; adapt the dimension contract and evaluate on independent queries. Do not relabel these authored values as learned embeddings. Hybrid fusion, neural reranking, persistent storage, quantization, and training are outside this workbook.

Primary reading: [Sentence-BERT](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10084), [Faiss metrics](https://github.com/facebookresearch/faiss/wiki/MetricType-and-distances), [Faiss indexes](https://github.com/facebookresearch/faiss/wiki/Faiss-indexes).
